description: In eval_script, the match on eval_stmt_list returns: None | Some(StmtResult::Continue) | Some(StmtResult::Stop) => actions.push(SieveAction::Keep). RFC 5228 §3.3 says stop halts execution but does NOT affect the implicit-keep rule — if no explicit disposition was reached before stop, Keep is correct. However, if a fileinto fired and then a stop occurred in a subsequent branch, the code correctly handles this because fileinto returns StmtResult::FileInto which exits eval_stmt_list before Stop can be produced. The subtle issue: Stop and None/Continue are aliased together, so a script that produces explicit Keep THEN calls stop in a nested block would correctly return Keep from the inner eval_stmt_list call, bubbling up through the outer. This appears correct on inspection but the Stop case in eval_script merging with None (no-action) hides the distinction between 'script ran stop with no prior disposition' and 'script naturally completed with no disposition'. Needs a test: stop before any disposition must produce Keep.
title: sieve: stop inside if-block returns Keep, not the script's last explicit action
